acceptanceCriteria: docs/specs/local-completion-policy-v0.md (or task-context-packet-v0.md) specifies the mention grammar with numbered requirements: at least `path:line`, `path:line-line`, `path#symbol`, a full or abbreviated commit SHA, and a requirement ID; each form names its resolution rule and its refusal codes.

Each form resolves to evidence pinned to the bound revision or reports `anchor-not-found`, ambiguous or `qualification-unverified`; no form is resolved lexically and no pronoun or transcript resolution is claimed.
The prompt-context path reports a resolved state instead of `explicit-task-anchor-required` when a task string carries a valid mention, with unit vectors for every form and every refusal.
The daily-loop UC-TASK-ORIENTATION cases gain at least one mention-anchored case and the frozen evaluation does not regress.
body: Filed 2026-09-23 from the owner's review of JetBrains Air (jetbrains.com/air, JetBrains blog 2026-09-22): the owner accepted the idea for 1.0. Air is a cloud/IDE orchestration platform; only its contracts transfer. Invariant 7 (AGENTS.md) still holds: no hosted service, UI, daemon or network dependency on the local path. Air lets a developer define a task by mentioning a specific line, commit, class, method or other symbol so the agent gets precise context instead of pasted text. Corvint already refuses unanchored tasks: LCP-V0-010 (docs/specs/local-completion-policy-v0.md:180) reports `explicit-task-anchor-required` without a path, requirement ID or source-backed identifier, and `anchor-not-found` when the anchor misses (this session's hook did both). A small mention grammar turns host-native mentions into deterministic pinned anchors. Related but distinct: V1-0118 (one-hop expansion from a resolved anchor).
title: context: accept structured task mentions (path:line, path#symbol, commit, requirement ID) as explicit task anchors
